newsitem.title: GERMANY: German April import prices dip as oil costs fall.
newsitem.headline: German April import prices dip as oil costs fall.

text.p: German import prices slipped 0.2 percent month-on-month in April as declining oil prices offset sharp increases in the coffee market, the Federal Statistics Office said on Monday.
On a year-on-year basis, import prices rose 2.1 percent, largely due to the 13 percent rise in the dollar since last year.
Crude oil prices in April fell 8.2 percent and petroleum product price 3.1 percent. At the same time, coffee prices climbed 12 percent.
Import prices in March were unchanged from February, when high winter oil prices combined with the strong dollar to push the official index up to the highest level since 1991.
April export prices rose 0.3 percent month-on-month and one percent year-on-year, the statistics office said.
The Bundesbank uses import prices to guage inflation pressure.
